summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for an exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis, presenting with severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, leading to inability to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with her standard IV pain and nausea regimen, including Dilaudid, Phenergan, and Ondansetron, along with IV fluids. Due to difficult venous access, a right PICC line was placed on hospital day one, which functioned well throughout the stay. Her warfarin was held initially due to inability to take oral medications, and she was bridged with enoxaparin. Oral intake was gradually advanced from clear liquids to solids by day four, and her home medications, including lisinopril, amitriptyline, and methadone, were restarted as tolerated. Her INR remained subtherapeutic at 1.1 upon discharge despite increased warfarin dosing, so she was discharged on continued enoxaparin with instructions to monitor INR and hold injections only once therapeutic levels were sustained. She also received support for anxiety and mild depression, and her J-tube site was monitored for signs of infection, though no active infection was found. She improved clinically, was ambulatory, and discharged home with follow-up arranged.
problems: Chronic venous embolism and thrombosis of internal jugular veins
